overall: Atlanta reached a running maximum of 91.4°F by around 16:19 ET, slightly above the NWS forecast high of 90°F, before a rapid storm-driven collapse dropped temperatures to 80.6°F by 17:49 ET — a plunge of nearly 11°F in roughly one hour. Active severe thunderstorm activity, including a Tornado Warning and Severe Thunderstorm Watch covering parts of northern Georgia, has firmly ended the afternoon heating cycle. The -9.0°F/hr velocity and -14.4°F/hr 30-minute velocity confirm an aggressive cooling trend with no likelihood of recovery.
forecast_obs_notes: All three NWP models (ECMWF=87.5°F, HRRR=89.6°F, NBM=86.8°F) underforecast today's actual peak, with even the warmest model (HRRR) coming in 1.8°F below the observed running max of 91.4°F. The give-up classifier fired at hour 14.67 when running max stood at 89.6°F, but temperatures continued rising for roughly 90 more minutes before the storm-driven collapse; the intraday model's 96.8% concentration in the 90-91°F bucket closely aligns with the observed outcome.
max_temp_prediction: The daily TMAX is effectively locked at 91.4°F with very high confidence. The hour of maximum has passed (16:19 ET), temperatures are collapsing at nearly 9–14°F/hr due to convective storm outflow, and active severe weather will persist through at least 23:00 ET per the Severe Thunderstorm Watch, precluding any rebound. The 90-91°F INTRADAY bucket at 96.8% is consistent with this reading, and the running max has been flat since ~17:00 ET.
